title: Apple Going Lower Led By Fakebook | Zero Hedge | Zero Hedge
text:
Summary
Facebook and Apple have a lot of room to go down further.
Both stocks are valued based on a huge amount of hype, faith, hope, call it what you want it's not solid financial analysis.
These 2 companies are in different tech businesses, but both have fueled their stock price based on the same part of the human brain.
We have been writing about Apple ( AAPL ) going down for years. None of our analysis was ever taken seriously or published so now that Apple ( AAPL ) has taken a substantial beating we thought it might be appropriate to chime in here. Our view on Apple ( AAPL ) is similar to Facebook ( FB ) we call "Fake Book" as it is based on mostly fake accounts, used by fake people, and depicts a fake world (you know that before someone posts a photo on Facebook they stage it well - it's not 'real' ).
Our opinion about Apple ( AAPL ) is simple; it's a great company that makes great products but is highly overvalued. Take a look at the biggest companies in the world based on market cap:
Now compare it with the more eclectic mix from 2007:
Energy, Automotive, Telecoms, Banks, Software.. A healthy mix. This is what an economy should look like. Of course you will all say "That was before the crisis" - let us assure you of one thing. Apple ( AAPL ) can't run the global economy, it takes oil and cars and boats and more. Until Apple ( AAPL ) gets into shipping or something useful we can say the following:
It is possible to live without Apple ( AAPL ) - it's not possible to live without Energy. Food & Energy is excluded from the CPI because these are the 2 things you can't live without.
As a side note, there is no question that Apple ( AAPL ) makes great products. iPhones have great cameras, that allow any user to be a professional photographer. Battery life and other features outperform most Android competitors. Apple laptops can last 10 years and still work! They don't get viruses. They make a lot of very high quality computers.
There is something real to the 'Cult of Mac' phenomenon. Just like Bitcoin ( BTC-USD ) is inflated based on hopes, dreams, and other irrational desires - so is Apple ( AAPL ).
Facebook ( FB )
Here again, we believe that FB can shrink by 90% and still be viable. Obviously it is the dominant social media platform and likely will be for some time. But as we have seen in the recent scandal , "Facebook" is not what it claims to be. They say one thing, and do another. They are sneaky, dishonest, and arrogant. And that's not good for investors! Look at the problems Elon Musk has created with his difficult personality.
Let's discuss what we know internally which has been confirmed with public info. After about 1 year of operation, software developers began to build 'bots' that would use Facebook 'automatically.' Facebook knew about this and allowed it because it boosted their numbers. The social bot industry grew so quickly and rapidly, because of the value of an account with 5,000 real followers for example, an entire black market emerged selling of such accounts. Like a web programmer may build up a site's traffic and sell it on flippa.com sites popped up that was like a marketplace of Facebook accounts. Here's a good article to read on this topic "The Bot Bubble" which claims:
..and that the market for Facebook spam was worth $87 million to $390 million.
$390 Million and this article is 3 years old! As we have done our own internet marketing and have participated in this business ourselves, we can say that:
1) Whatever figures are out there are only a fraction of what it really is, because it's very hard to gauge what's real and what's not in a big data sense.
2) It is in the interest of Facebook ( FB ) to support the spam bot culture as Facebook relies on mass amounts of content and big number growth - especially for advertisers $$$
3) If you remove the bots, the spam, the low quality nothing accounts and posts - you're taking away 90% of Facebook ( FB ) numbers.
What's the 10%? The 10% are the real power users, the Grandmas that use Facebook ( FB ) to keep in touch with relatives, the business users, families, just regular people using it.
The inflated numbers that claim Facebook ( FB ) has 2.7 Billion users is interesting, but largely irrelevant. How many people signed up for an account and never used it? How many are bots? How many are fake accounts?
Those in the internet marketing space may open 10 - 100 accounts for themselves, Facebook ( FB ) is not doing KYC on new account holders they are only verifying a mobile phone, but getting a mobile number or 10,000 of them is not difficult it's just a question of buying them.
So, in conclusion - we are claiming that eventually - and it may take years to realize this - but this will all be realized in the stock price. Facebook ( FB ) is not THE ONLY social media on the planet, users have moved to Twitter and regional platforms. It can be sparked by a scandal like we saw this year or a law change, or any number of factors. It's going to happen, Facebook ( FB ) has served it's purpose and is now no longer needed. Crypto is the new tool.
Last thought - why no mention of US Government control of Facebook ( FB ) in the Congressional hearings? The Snowden leak not only identified Facebook ( FB ) in the PRISM program, but it indicated that Facebook ( FB ) is the PRIMARY tool of surveillance used by the US intelligence agencies. One of the original investors into Facebook ( FB ) was the CIA through the VC arm IN-Q-TEL.
Yet none of this was mentioned in the hearings, in which Facebook ( FB ) was being accused of collecting and using customer data?
Why others are different
Other big cap techs like Amazon ( AMZN ), Google ( GOOGL ), Microsoft ( MSFT ), IBM ( IBM ), etc. are completely different.
Google ( GOOGL ) although also implicated in the PRISM scandal, and also had funding by IN-Q-TEL - but Google ( GOOGL ) has a much more robust and viable business model. Not only is Google ( GOOGL ) the king of search, they have dominated multiple verticals by using their search dominance to gain market share, and at the end of the day - they offer a really good advertising marketplace which is the core of their business. While Facebook ( FB ) originally took ad revenue away from Google ( GOOGL ) it seems there will be a reversal of that trend, and also towards Amazon (NASDAQ: AMZN ) ads which are only now starting to be popular.
We're not short, but this is for the record - if you're long, it's a good time to take your profits and look for other long term performers - there are so many. Both Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) and Facebook ( FB ) have stocks that are over inflated due to the hype-n-hope machine which lasts for a time, but ultimately it always pops - just look at Crypto.
